11: <!-- SPECKIT_TEMPLATE_SOURCE: plan-core | v2.2 -->
12: # Implementation Plan: Phase 1: template-drift-census-and-baseline
13: 
14: <!-- SPECKIT_LEVEL: 3 -->
15: 
16: ---
17: 
18: <!-- ANCHOR:summary -->
19: ## 1. SUMMARY
20: 
21: ### Technical Context
22: 
23: | Aspect | Value |
24: |--------|-------|
25: | **Language/Stack** | Markdown, Bash, ripgrep, awk, jq |
26: | **Framework** | system-spec-kit validator and scaffold scripts |
27: | **Storage** | JSONL files in this phase's `scratch/` |
28: | **Testing** | Each ledger row carries its own reproduce command |
29: 
30: ### Overview
31: Three DeepSeek workers each read one directory set and write candidate defect rows. The conductor re-runs every row's evidence command and keeps only the rows that reproduce. Then three workers each author the same small Level 2 packet in a throwaway track, and the conductor measures the result with fixed commands.
32: <!-- /ANCHOR:summary -->
33: 
34: ---
35: 
36: <!-- ANCHOR:quality-gates -->
37: ## 2. QUALITY GATES
38: 
39: ### Definition of Ready
40: - [ ] The launch preconditions in `../spec.md` section 3 are recorded as met in `../goal.md` section 4
41: - [ ] `tasks.md` T001 to T003 are done: provider check, worktree check, start commit recorded
42: 
43: ### Definition of Done
44: - [ ] Every row in `acceptance-criteria.md` is `Met`
45: - [ ] `bash .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/validate.sh <this phase> --strict` prints `RESULT: PASSED`
46: - [ ] `git status --porcelain` lists nothing outside this phase folder
47: <!-- /ANCHOR:quality-gates -->
48: 
49: ---
50: 
51: <!-- ANCHOR:architecture -->
52: ## 3. ARCHITECTURE
53: 
54: ### Pattern
55: Fan-out of read-only lanes, then a deterministic reduce by the conductor.
56: 
57: ### Key Components
58: - **Lane A worker**: reads `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/` except `examples/`.
59: - **Lane B worker**: reads `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/examples/`.
60: - **Lane C worker**: reads `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/references/templates/`, `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/references/workflows/` and `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/SKILL.md`.
61: - **Conductor**: merges lane files, re-runs evidence, writes `ledger.jsonl`, runs the baseline.
62: 
63: ### Ledger schema (frozen)
64: 
65: One JSON object per line. All ten fields are required strings.
66: 
67: | Field | Meaning |
68: |-------|---------|
69: | `id` | `L-<lane>-<NNN>`, for example `L-B-004` |
70: | `lane` | `A`, `B` or `C` |
71: | `file` | Repository-relative path of the file with the defect |
72: | `locator` | Exact text that occurs once in that file and marks the defect |
73: | `defect_class` | One of the eight classes below |
74: | `observed` | What is there now, in one sentence |
75: | `expected_text` | The exact replacement text, or `DELETE FILE`, or `OWNED BY PHASE` when a later phase rewrites the area |
76: | `owner_phase` | `002`, `003`, `004`, `005`, `006` or `041-006` |
77: | `evidence_cmd` | One shell command, run from the repository root |
78: | `evidence_expect` | The exact text or count that command prints while the defect exists |
79: 
80: ### Defect classes and detection commands
81: 
82: Run each from the repository root. `S=.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit`.
83: 
84: | Class | Detection command | Owner |
85: |-------|-------------------|-------|
86: | `leaked-description` | `rg -n '^description: "([a-z]|.*-->)' $S/templates` | 002 |
87: | `stale-reference` | `rg -o --no-filename '\.skilled/[A-Za-z0-9_./+-]+' <dir> \| sort -u \| while read p; do test -e "$p" \|\| echo "MISSING $p"; done` and `rg -n -i 'checklist\.md' <dir>` | 002 |
88: | `unresolved-placeholder` | `rg -n '<spec-folder>\|<path>\|<track>' <dir>` on prose lines outside code blocks | 002 or 041-006 |
89: | `self-contradiction` | Read the file. Report two lines that state opposite rules for the same thing | 002 |
90: | `dead-file` | For each non-markdown file at `$S/templates/` top level: `rg -l --hidden "<basename>" .skilled --glob '!<that file>' \| wc -l` prints `0` | 002 |
91: | `gate-anchor-crossing` | `awk 'BEGIN{d=0} /<!-- IF /{d++} /<!-- \/IF -->/{d--} /<!-- ANCHOR:/{match($0,/ANCHOR:[a-z0-9-]+/); a[substr($0,RSTART+7,RLENGTH-7)]=d} /<!-- \/ANCHOR:/{match($0,/ANCHOR:[a-z0-9-]+/); n=substr($0,RSTART+7,RLENGTH-7); if (a[n]!=d) print FILENAME":"NR": anchor "n" opens at "a[n]" closes at "d}' <file.tmpl>` | 004 |
92: | `unenforced-hint` | `rg -c '\[[A-Za-z][^]\[]{2,}\]' $S/templates/core/*.tmpl` | 003 |
93: | `doc-code-mismatch` | `rg -n '\[PLACEHOLDER\]' $S/references` and any reference sentence that names a rule `validate.sh` does not run | 003 |
94: 
95: ### The five confirmed defects (must appear as rows)
96: 
97: | # | File | Locator | Class | Owner |
98: |---|------|---------|-------|-------|
99: | 1 | `$S/templates/examples/level-2/tasks.md` and 17 other example docs | `description: "including effort estimates and explicit verification tasks for each feature. -->"` | `leaked-description` | 002 |
100: | 2 | `$S/templates/examples/level-2/tasks.md`, `level-3/tasks.md`, `level-3+/tasks.md` | `- [x] Checklist.md fully verified` | `stale-reference` | 002 |
101: | 3 | `$S/references/workflows/spec-folder-write-recipe.md` | `  <spec-folder>` | `unresolved-placeholder` | 041-006 |
102: | 4 | `$S/references/workflows/spec-folder-authoring-checklist.md` | ``such as `<spec-folder>`.`` | `unresolved-placeholder` | 002 |
103: | 5 | `$S/references/templates/template-style-guide.md` | `### Why Bulleted Lists` | `self-contradiction` | 002 |
104: 
105: Defect 1 is one row per example file, 18 rows in all. The other confirmed items, `templates/.hashes` as a dead file and the anchor crossings in `spec.md.tmpl`, are expected from the lane commands and need no special handling.
106: 
107: ### Data Flow
108: Lane brief, then lane JSONL, then conductor reproduce check, then `ledger.jsonl`, then frontier review, then the final `ledger.jsonl` that phase 2 reads.
109: <!-- /ANCHOR:architecture -->

114: ## FIX ADDENDUM: AFFECTED SURFACES
115: 
116: This phase changes no producer or consumer. The table records what it reads so the census can be checked for coverage.

118: | Surface | Current Role | Action | Verification |

122: | `references/templates`, `references/workflows`, `SKILL.md` | Authoring guidance and router | unchanged, read by lane C | lane C JSONL read line |

125: - Same-class producers: every class in section 3 has a command that runs over the whole lane directory, not one file.
126: - Consumers of changed symbols: none, nothing changes.

293: ## AI EXECUTION PROTOCOL
294: 
295: Written for the executing swarm. Follow each rule as written. Where a rule and your own judgment disagree, follow the rule and record the disagreement in `goal.md` section 4.
296: 
297: ### Roles
298: - **Conductor**: one DeepSeek V4.1 Flash max session that is not itself running inside OpenCode, because `cli-opencode` refuses a dispatch from inside OpenCode. It dispatches workers, runs every verify command, edits only this phase folder, and keeps `goal.md` section 4 current.
299: - **Worker**: one `opencode2 run` dispatch on `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max`. One worker does one lane or one baseline run, then stops.
300: - **Reviewer**: one read-only frontier review through `cli-codex` at phase close. It writes nothing.
301: 
302: ### Pre-Task Checklist
303: - [ ] Read this phase's `spec.md`, this plan and `tasks.md` before the first dispatch
304: - [ ] Read `.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/SKILL.md` sections 3 and 4 before composing the first worker command
305: - [ ] Confirm the working directory is the build worktree recorded in `../goal.md` section 4, never the main checkout
306: - [ ] Confirm `opencode2 models --standalone` lists `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`
307: - [ ] Save every brief to `scratch/briefs/<task-id>.txt` before dispatching it
308: 
309: ### Execution Rules
310: 
311: | Rule | Requirement |
312: |------|-------------|
313: | TASK-SEQ | Run tasks in ID order. Tasks marked `[P]` may run together, at most three at once, and only when no two write the same file |
314: | TASK-SCOPE | A worker writes only the paths under ALLOWED WRITE PATHS in its brief |
315: | TASK-VERIFY | The conductor runs the task's verify command and reads both its output and its exit status before marking the task `[x]` |
316: | TASK-LOCATE | Find text by its exact content, never by a line number |
317: | TASK-BANNED | Workers never run `git commit`, `git push`, `git checkout`, `git switch`, `git branch`, `git reset`, `git stash`, `generate-context.js` or `/speckit:save` |
318: 
319: ### Worker Brief Skeleton
320: 
321: Every brief starts with this block, word for word, with the two paths filled in:
322: 
323: ```text
324: GATE 3 IS PRE-RESOLVED. DO NOT ASK THE DOCUMENTATION-SCOPE QUESTION.
325: 
326: You are a non-interactive dispatched worker. AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 and
327: SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 are set in your environment, which this repository's AGENTS.md
328: defines as the autonomous child-dispatch exemption: the spec-folder question is pre-resolved
329: and MUST NOT be asked. No answer can reach you, because nobody is at a prompt.
330: 
331: Your write authority is already bound. The spec folder is:
332:   specs/system-speckit/054-weak-model-spec-authoring/001-template-drift-census-and-baseline
333: 
334: Proceed directly to the work. Do not print A/B/C/D options. Do not stop to confirm anything.
335: A failed edit match means a stale anchor: re-read the file and retry; halt only after three
336: failures on the same file.
337: Your task is complete only when files exist on disk and the verification command has been run.
338: 
339: ROLE: You are a read-only auditor. You read files, run read-only commands and write one
340: result file. Your output is checked line by line by a script.
341: 
342: ALLOWED WRITE PATHS:
343:   <the one file this task names>
344: 
345: BANNED OPERATIONS: git commit, git push, git checkout, git switch, git branch, git reset,
346: git stash, rm, mv, create.sh outside the task's stated command, generate-context.js,
347: /speckit:save, and any edit to a file not listed under ALLOWED WRITE PATHS.
348: ```
349: 
350: The role line is a focused persona summary in place of a full agent file, the small-context exception that `cli-opencode` rule 18 allows. It is declared here as that exception.
351: 
352: ### Dispatch Command
353: 
354: ```bash
355: cd "$WORKTREE" && SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 opencode2 run --standalone \
356:   -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max --format json \
357:   "$(cat "$PHASE/scratch/briefs/$TASK.txt")" </dev/null > "$PHASE/scratch/runs/$TASK.jsonl" 2>&1 &
358: PID=$!; wait "$PID"; kill -9 "$PID" 2>/dev/null; pkill -9 -P "$PID" 2>/dev/null
359: ```
360: 
361: `PHASE` is this folder's path and `WORKTREE` is the build worktree. Never kill by a name pattern. Kill only the captured PID.
362: 
363: ### Status Reporting Format
364: 
365: `[T###] DONE | BLOCKED - one line of evidence`, written as a row in the progress table of `goal.md` section 4.
366: 
367: ### Blocked Task Protocol
368: 1. Restore any file the task changed with `git restore --source=<start commit> -- <file>`.
369: 2. Mark the task `[B]` in `tasks.md` with the failing command and the first line of its output.
370: 3. Re-dispatch at most twice with the brief corrected for what failed. After the third failure on the same task, leave it `[B]` and continue with the next task.
371: 4. Stop the phase when two tasks are blocked, and write `STOP` with both task IDs in `goal.md` section 4.

376: ## L3: ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORD
377: 
378: ### ADR-001: Keep only rows that reproduce
379: 
380: **Status**: Accepted
381: 
382: **Context**: A DeepSeek worker asked to find defects will also report things that are not defects.
383: 
384: **Decision**: A lane row enters `ledger.jsonl` only when the conductor runs its `evidence_cmd` on the unchanged tree and the output contains its `evidence_expect`. The `self-contradiction` class has no command, so those rows go to the frontier review instead.
385: 
386: **Consequences**:
387: - Phase 2 receives no row it cannot reproduce.
388: - A real defect the worker described badly is dropped. The frontier review reads the source files again to catch those.
389: 
390: **Alternatives Rejected**:
391: - Trusting lane output as written: it puts unconfirmed findings into a repair phase that edits shared templates.
392: 
393: ### ADR-002: One fixed authoring task, three runs, run in a throwaway track
394: 
395: **Status**: Accepted
396: 
397: **Context**: The baseline must be rerun unchanged in phase 8, and one run of a sampling model is one sample.
398: 
399: **Decision**: The task text in `tasks.md` T009 is frozen. It runs three times per side. Each run creates `specs/zz-bench-authoring/`, and the conductor deletes that directory after measuring.
400: 
401: **Consequences**:
402: - Phase 8 compares like with like and reports a range.
403: - Three runs cannot detect a small effect. Phase 8 reports the range, not a significance claim.
404: 
405: **Alternatives Rejected**:
406: - Measuring by a frontier model's judgment of quality: one model is one opinion, and the five metrics are commands.

345: BANNED OPERATIONS: git commit, git push, git checkout, git switch, git branch, git reset,
346: git stash, rm, mv, create.sh outside the task's stated command, generate-context.js,
347: /speckit:save, and any edit to a file not listed under ALLOWED WRITE PATHS.
348: ```
349: 
350: The role line is a focused persona summary in place of a full agent file, the small-context exception that `cli-opencode` rule 18 allows. It is declared here as that exception.
351: 
352: ### Dispatch Command
353: 
354: ```bash
355: cd "$WORKTREE" && SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 opencode2 run --standalone \
356:   -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max --format json \
357:   "$(cat "$PHASE/scratch/briefs/$TASK.txt")" </dev/null > "$PHASE/scratch/runs/$TASK.jsonl" 2>&1 &
358: PID=$!; wait "$PID"; kill -9 "$PID" 2>/dev/null; pkill -9 -P "$PID" 2>/dev/null
359: ```
360: 
361: `PHASE` is this folder's path and `WORKTREE` is the build worktree. Never kill by a name pattern. Kill only the captured PID.
362: 
363: ### Status Reporting Format
364: 
365: `[T###] DONE | BLOCKED - one line of evidence`, written as a row in the progress table of `goal.md` section 4.
366: 
367: ### Blocked Task Protocol
368: 1. Restore any file the task changed with `git restore --source=<start commit> -- <file>`.
369: 2. Mark the task `[B]` in `tasks.md` with the failing command and the first line of its output.
370: 3. Re-dispatch at most twice with the brief corrected for what failed. After the third failure on the same task, leave it `[B]` and continue with the next task.
371: 4. Stop the phase when two tasks are blocked, and write `STOP` with both task IDs in `goal.md` section 4.

376: ## L3: ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORD
377: 
378: ### ADR-001: Keep only rows that reproduce
379: 
380: **Status**: Accepted
381: 
382: **Context**: A DeepSeek worker asked to find defects will also report things that are not defects.
383: 
384: **Decision**: A lane row enters `ledger.jsonl` only when the conductor runs its `evidence_cmd` on the unchanged tree and the output contains its `evidence_expect`. The `self-contradiction` class has no command, so those rows go to the frontier review instead.
385: 
386: **Consequences**:
387: - Phase 2 receives no row it cannot reproduce.
388: - A real defect the worker described badly is dropped. The frontier review reads the source files again to catch those.
389: 
390: **Alternatives Rejected**:
391: - Trusting lane output as written: it puts unconfirmed findings into a repair phase that edits shared templates.
392: 
393: ### ADR-002: One fixed authoring task, three runs, run in a throwaway track
394: 
395: **Status**: Accepted
396: 
397: **Context**: The baseline must be rerun unchanged in phase 8, and one run of a sampling model is one sample.
398: 
399: **Decision**: The task text in `tasks.md` T009 is frozen. It runs three times per side. Each run creates `specs/zz-bench-authoring/`, and the conductor deletes that directory after measuring.
400: 
401: **Consequences**:
402: - Phase 8 compares like with like and reports a range.
403: - Three runs cannot detect a small effect. Phase 8 reports the range, not a significance claim.
404: 
405: **Alternatives Rejected**:
406: - Measuring by a frontier model's judgment of quality: one model is one opinion, and the five metrics are commands.

14: # Spec Folder Write Recipe
15: 
16: ## 1. OVERVIEW
17: 
18: When `/speckit:complete` or any other workflow needs to write a new spec folder, this recipe is the canonical path. Follow each step in order. Each step has a verification gate.
19: 
20: ---
21: 
22: ## 2. PRE-CONDITIONS
23: 
24: - Spec folder track decided (e.g., `skilled-agent-orchestration/`, `00--ai-systems/`, etc.)

27:

29: 
30: ## 3. STEPS
31: 
32: ### Step 1: Scaffold via create.sh
33: 
34: Run the system-spec-kit scaffold from the repository root:
35: 
36: ```bash
37: bash .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/create.sh \
38:   --skip-branch \
39:   --short-name "opencode-authoring-recipe" \
40:   --number 078 \
41:   --level 1
42: ```
43: 
44: Verification gate: confirm the scaffolded folder exists and contains the expected Level contract files.
45: 
46: ### Step 2: Move to track
47: 
48: Move the scaffolded folder from the default location into the selected track, for example:
49: 
50: ```bash
51: mv specs/078-opencode-authoring-recipe \
52:   <spec-folder>
53: ```
54: 
55: Verification gate: confirm the final path is under `specs/` or `.opencode/specs/` and matches the packet pointer.
56: 
57: ### Step 3: Author 4 Level-1 docs
58: 
59: - `spec.md` (7 anchors: metadata, problem, scope, requirements, success-criteria, risks, questions)
60: - `plan.md` (7 anchors: summary, quality-gates, architecture, phases, testing, dependencies, rollback)
61: - `tasks.md` (6 anchors: notation, phase-1, phase-2, phase-3, completion, cross-refs; phase headers MUST be canonical "Phase 1: Setup" / "Phase 2: Implementation" / "Phase 3: Verification")
62: - `implementation-summary.md` (6 anchors: metadata, what-built, how-delivered, decisions, verification, limitations)
63: 
64: Verification gate: run `rg -n "ANCHOR:" <folder>` and confirm each doc has the full anchor count.
65: 
66: ### Step 4: Frontmatter `_memory.continuity` block
67: 
68: - `packet_pointer`: slash-separated relative path (NOT just folder name)
69: - `recent_action`: keep compact (NOT verbose multi-clause)
70: - `last_updated_at`: ISO-8601 UTC
71: 
72: Verification gate: run `rg -n "_memory:|packet_pointer|recent_action|last_updated_at" <folder>`.
73: 
74: ### Step 5: Refresh metadata
75: 
76: ```bash
77: node .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/dist/spec-folder/generate-description.js \
78:   <folder> \
79:   <repo-root> \
80:   --description "Short description for memory search" \
81:   --level N
82: 
83: node .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/dist/graph/backfill-graph-metadata.js \
84:   <folder>
85: ```
86: 
87: Verification gate: confirm `description.json` and `graph-metadata.json` exist and describe the same folder.
88: 
89: ### Step 6: validate.sh --strict gate
90: 
91: ```bash
92: bash .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/validate.sh <folder> --strict
93: ```
94: 
95: Must print `RESULT: PASSED` with 0 errors. A warning does not fail `--strict`, so read each one and fix the ones that are real.
96: 
97: Common pitfalls: `SPECDOC_SUFFICIENCY_004` (research.md needs anchor + citation pattern), `TEMPLATE_HEADERS` (canonical phase header names required), `ANCHORS_VALID` (full 7/7/6/6 anchor count per doc-type).
98: 
99: ### Step 7: Commit + push
100: 
101: - Workspace: use the one the operator chose, a worktree or the current branch. Never pick it yourself and never create a branch with git primitives (see "Workspace Choice Enforcement" in `.skilled/skills/sk-git/SKILL.md`). `main` is on the remote allowlist, so pushing it needs no extra approval, and a branch off the allowlist needs the operator's go-ahead for that push (see "Remote Push Permission Enforcement" in the same file).
102: - Subject: `type(subsystem): summary`. Take the type from the first match in the priority list in `.skilled/skills/sk-git/SKILL.md` (a doc-only packet is `docs`) and name the owning subsystem as the scope, such as `spec-kit`. Never use the packet number or path as the scope.
103: - Body: at least one prose line that says why. Trailers do not count as a body.
104: - Trailers: `Spec: <track>/<packet>`, the packet's path below `specs/` without the `specs/` segment. `prepare-commit-msg` stamps `Commit-Id:`, so never type it.
105: - No attribution trailers. The `commit-msg` hook refuses `Co-Authored-By:` and `Claude-Session:`.
106: 
107: The full contract is `.skilled/skills/sk-git/assets/commit-message-template.md`.
108:

In a shared tree `git status --short` also lists other sessions' changes, so it cannot be the test (see "Step 7: Scoped-Staging Discipline" in `.skilled/skills/sk-git/references/commit-workflows.md`).

14: # Spec Folder Write Recipe
15: 
16: ## 1. OVERVIEW
17: 
18: When `/speckit:complete` or any other workflow needs to write a new spec folder, this recipe is the canonical path. Follow each step in order. Each step has a verification gate.
19: 
20: ---
21: 
22: ## 2. PRE-CONDITIONS
23: 
24: - Spec folder track decided (e.g., `skilled-agent-orchestration/`, `00--ai-systems/`, etc.)
25: - Next packet number known (highest `[0-9][0-9][0-9]-*` + 1 in track)
26: - Documentation level decided (Level 1, 2, 3, or 3+)
27: 
28: ---
29: 
30: ## 3. STEPS
31: 
32: ### Step 1: Scaffold via create.sh
33: 
34: Run the system-spec-kit scaffold from the repository root:
35: 
36: ```bash
37: bash .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/create.sh \
38:   --skip-branch \
39:   --short-name "opencode-authoring-recipe" \
40:   --number 078 \
41:   --level 1
42: ```
43: 
44: Verification gate: confirm the scaffolded folder exists and contains the expected Level contract files.
45: 
46: ### Step 2: Move to track
47: 
48: Move the scaffolded folder from the default location into the selected track, for example:
49: 
50: ```bash
51: mv specs/078-opencode-authoring-recipe \
52:   <spec-folder>
53: ```
54: 
55: Verification gate: confirm the final path is under `specs/` or `.opencode/specs/` and matches the packet pointer.
56: 
57: ### Step 3: Author 4 Level-1 docs
58: 
59: - `spec.md` (7 anchors: metadata, problem, scope, requirements, success-criteria, risks, questions)
60: - `plan.md` (7 anchors: summary, quality-gates, architecture, phases, testing, dependencies, rollback)
61: - `tasks.md` (6 anchors: notation, phase-1, phase-2, phase-3, completion, cross-refs; phase headers MUST be canonical "Phase 1: Setup" / "Phase 2: Implementation" / "Phase 3: Verification")
62: - `implementation-summary.md` (6 anchors: metadata, what-built, how-delivered, decisions, verification, limitations)
63: 
64: Verification gate: run `rg -n "ANCHOR:" <folder>` and confirm each doc has the full anchor count.
65: 
66: ### Step 4: Frontmatter `_memory.continuity` block
67: 
68: - `packet_pointer`: slash-separated relative path (NOT just folder name)
69: - `recent_action`: keep compact (NOT verbose multi-clause)
70: - `last_updated_at`: ISO-8601 UTC
71: 
72: Verification gate: run `rg -n "_memory:|packet_pointer|recent_action|last_updated_at" <folder>`.
73: 
74: ### Step 5: Refresh metadata
75: 
76: ```bash
77: node .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/dist/spec-folder/generate-description.js \
78:   <folder> \
79:   <repo-root> \
80:   --description "Short description for memory search" \
81:   --level N
82: 
83: node .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/dist/graph/backfill-graph-metadata.js \
84:   <folder>
85: ```
86: 
87: Verification gate: confirm `description.json` and `graph-metadata.json` exist and describe the same folder.
88: 
89: ### Step 6: validate.sh --strict gate
90: 
91: ```bash
92: bash .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/validate.sh <folder> --strict
93: ```
94: 
95: Must print `RESULT: PASSED` with 0 errors. A warning does not fail `--strict`, so read each one and fix the ones that are real.
96: 
97: Common pitfalls: `SPECDOC_SUFFICIENCY_004` (research.md needs anchor + citation pattern), `TEMPLATE_HEADERS` (canonical phase header names required), `ANCHORS_VALID` (full 7/7/6/6 anchor count per doc-type).
98: 
99: ### Step 7: Commit + push
100: 
101: - Workspace: use the one the operator chose, a worktree or the current branch. Never pick it yourself and never create a branch with git primitives (see "Workspace Choice Enforcement" in `.skilled/skills/sk-git/SKILL.md`). `main` is on the remote allowlist, so pushing it needs no extra approval, and a branch off the allowlist needs the operator's go-ahead for that push (see "Remote Push Permission Enforcement" in the same file).
102: - Subject: `type(subsystem): summary`. Take the type from the first match in the priority list in `.skilled/skills/sk-git/SKILL.md` (a doc-only packet is `docs`) and name the owning subsystem as the scope, such as `spec-kit`. Never use the packet number or path as the scope.
103: - Body: at least one prose line that says why. Trailers do not count as a body.
104: - Trailers: `Spec: <track>/<packet>`, the packet's path below `specs/` without the `specs/` segment. `prepare-commit-msg` stamps `Commit-Id:`, so never type it.
105: - No attribution trailers. The `commit-msg` hook refuses `Co-Authored-By:` and `Claude-Session:`.
106: 
107: The full contract is `.skilled/skills/sk-git/assets/commit-message-template.md`.
108: 
109: Verification gate: stage the packet files by explicit path, then confirm `git diff --cached --name-only` lists only the intended packet files before commit. In a shared tree `git status --short` also lists other sessions' changes, so it cannot be the test (see "Step 7: Scoped-Staging Discipline" in `.skilled/skills/sk-git/references/commit-workflows.md`).

14: # Sub-Folder Versioning - Iterative Work Organization Pattern
15: 
16: Workflow-assisted pattern for organizing iterative work within existing spec folders using canonical packet continuity plus generated support artifacts.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Purpose
23: 
24: Enable clean separation of iterative work within a single spec folder while preserving historical context through packet continuity. Each iteration maintains its own canonical continuity (the `_memory.continuity` block in its `implementation-summary.md`) plus a git-ignored `scratch/` workspace tied to that child packet.
25: 
26: ### Important Note
27: 
28: Sub-folder versioning is **workflow-assisted**: the AI can suggest it during Option A flows and `create.sh --subfolder` creates numbered sub-folders with a `scratch/` directory and `graph-metadata.json` automatically. Legacy `[spec]/memory/*.md` artifacts are no longer produced. Existing root docs are not auto-moved; archival/reorganization remains explicit.
29: 
30: ### When to Use
31: 
32: - Working on distinct phases of the same feature
33: - Separating distinct but related iterations within the parent spec's documented scope; genuinely unrelated work belongs in a separate top-level packet
34: - Creating clear boundaries between implementation iterations
35: - Preserving context when returning to old work
36: 
37: ---
38: 
39: ## 2. DIRECTORY STRUCTURE
40: 
41: ```
42: specs/###-name/
43: ├── 001-original-topic/   # First iteration
44: │   ├── spec.md
45: │   ├── plan.md
46: │   ├── implementation-summary.md   # _memory.continuity block (canonical context)
47: │   └── scratch/                    # git-ignored working files
48: ├── 002-new-iteration/    # Second iteration
49: │   ├── spec.md
50: │   ├── plan.md
51: │   ├── implementation-summary.md
52: │   └── scratch/
53: └── 003-another-task/     # Third iteration (current, active)
54:     ├── spec.md
55:     ├── plan.md
56:     ├── implementation-summary.md   # Independent continuity
57:     └── scratch/
58: ```
59: 
60: ---
61: 
62: ## 3. WORKFLOW STEPS
63: 
64: ### Step 1: Recognition
65: 
66: When selecting Option A (existing folder), the AI agent checks for root-level content and suggests sub-folder organization if appropriate.
67: 
68: ### Step 2: User Decision
69: 
70: User decides whether to:
71: - **Create sub-folder**: Organize new work in a numbered sub-folder
72: - **Continue in root**: Keep working in the existing structure
73: 
74: ### Step 3: Manual Organization
75: 
76: If creating a sub-folder, the user (with AI guidance):
77: 1. Chooses a descriptive name for the sub-folder
78: 2. Creates the folder structure manually or via `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/create.sh --subfolder`
79: 3. Copies templates as needed
80: 
81: **Script-assisted example:**
82: 
83: ```bash
84: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/create.sh \
85:   --subfolder specs/<track> \
86:   --topic memory-overhaul \
87:   --level 3+ \
88:   "Wave 1 follow-up"
89: ```
90: 
91: ### Step 4: Path Tracking
92: 
93: Routine saves pass the target spec folder alongside structured JSON.
94: 
95: ---
96: 
97: ## 4. NAMING CONVENTION
98: 
99: - **Sub-folder format**: `{###}-{descriptive-name}` (script-generated or manual)
100: - **Numbers**: 001, 002, 003, etc. (3-digit padded, sequential)
101: - **Name rules**: lowercase, hyphens, 2-3 words (shorter is better)
102: - **Examples**: `001-mcp-code-mode`, `002-api-refactor`, `003-bug-fixes`
103: 
104: ---
105: 
106: ## 5. MEMORY CONTEXT ROUTING
107: 
108: - Spec folder path passed explicitly alongside structured JSON for routine saves
109: - `generate-context.js` refreshes canonical continuity in the specified sub-folder's `implementation-summary.md` `_memory.continuity` block (legacy `[spec]/memory/*.md` writes are retired)
110: - Each iteration has isolated continuity history
111: - Sub-folder creation also provisions isolated `scratch/` directories
112: - Older packets may still contain a root `memory/` directory from before the retirement; current saves write only canonical continuity
113: 
114: ---
115: 
116: ## 6. EXAMPLE USE CASE
117: 
118: ### Manual Sub-Folder Organization
119: 
120: **Scenario:** User wants to organize iterative work within an existing spec folder
121: 
122: 1. **Initial State:**
123:    ```
124:    specs/007-auth-system/
125:    ├── spec.md
126:    ├── plan.md
127:    └── implementation-summary.md
128:    ```
129: 
130: 2. **After Manual Organization:**
131:    ```
132:    specs/007-auth-system/
133:    ├── 001-initial-implementation/    # Original content (manually moved)
134:    │   ├── spec.md
135:    │   ├── plan.md
136:    │   └── implementation-summary.md
137:    └── 002-oauth-addition/            # New work
138:        ├── spec.md
139:        ├── plan.md
140:        └── implementation-summary.md
141:    ```
142: 
143: **Key Points:**
144: - User manually creates and organizes sub-folders
145: - Original content can be moved to a sub-folder if desired
146: - Each sub-folder has independent continuity in its `implementation-summary.md`
147: - Numbering is sequential within the spec folder
148: 
149: ### Step-by-Step Walkthrough
150: 
151: 1. User runs `/spec_kit:complete` or similar
152: 2. Gate 3 asks: "Spec folder?" → User selects **A) Existing**
153: 3. User selects `specs/007-auth-system/`
154: 4. AI suggests: "This folder has existing content. Would you like to organize work in a sub-folder?"
155: 5. If yes:
156:    - User provides sub-folder name: "002-oauth-addition"
157:    - AI helps create the sub-folder with templates
158:    - Continuity saves update the sub-folder's `implementation-summary.md` `_memory.continuity` block
159: 6. If no:
160:    - Continue working in root folder
161: 
162: ---
163: 
164: ## 7. BENEFITS
165: 
166: - Clean separation of iterative work
167: - Preserves all historical work (no data loss)
168: - Independent continuity per iteration
169: - Backward compatible (works with non-versioned folders)
170: - Flexible organization based on project needs

14: # Sub-Folder Versioning - Iterative Work Organization Pattern
15: 
16: Workflow-assisted pattern for organizing iterative work within existing spec folders using canonical packet continuity plus generated support artifacts.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Purpose
23: 
24: Enable clean separation of iterative work within a single spec folder while preserving historical context through packet continuity. Each iteration maintains its own canonical continuity (the `_memory.continuity` block in its `implementation-summary.md`) plus a git-ignored `scratch/` workspace tied to that child packet.
25: 
26: ### Important Note
27: 
28: Sub-folder versioning is **workflow-assisted**: the AI can suggest it during Option A flows and `create.sh --subfolder` creates numbered sub-folders with a `scratch/` directory and `graph-metadata.json` automatically. Legacy `[spec]/memory/*.md` artifacts are no longer produced. Existing root docs are not auto-moved; archival/reorganization remains explicit.
29: 
30: ### When to Use
31: 
32: - Working on distinct phases of the same feature
33: - Separating distinct but related iterations within the parent spec's documented scope; genuinely unrelated work belongs in a separate top-level packet
34: - Creating clear boundaries between implementation iterations
35: - Preserving context when returning to old work
36: 
37: ---
38: 
39: ## 2. DIRECTORY STRUCTURE
40: 
41: ```
42: specs/###-name/
43: ├── 001-original-topic/   # First iteration
44: │   ├── spec.md
45: │   ├── plan.md
46: │   ├── implementation-summary.md   # _memory.continuity block (canonical context)
47: │   └── scratch/                    # git-ignored working files
48: ├── 002-new-iteration/    # Second iteration
49: │   ├── spec.md
50: │   ├── plan.md
51: │   ├── implementation-summary.md
52: │   └── scratch/
53: └── 003-another-task/     # Third iteration (current, active)
54:     ├── spec.md
55:     ├── plan.md
56:     ├── implementation-summary.md   # Independent continuity
57:     └── scratch/
58: ```
59: 
60: ---
61: 
62: ## 3. WORKFLOW STEPS
63: 
64: ### Step 1: Recognition
65: 
66: When selecting Option A (existing folder), the AI agent checks for root-level content and suggests sub-folder organization if appropriate.
67: 
68: ### Step 2: User Decision
69: 
70: User decides whether to:
71: - **Create sub-folder**: Organize new work in a numbered sub-folder
72: - **Continue in root**: Keep working in the existing structure
73: 
74: ### Step 3: Manual Organization
75: 
76: If creating a sub-folder, the user (with AI guidance):
77: 1. Chooses a descriptive name for the sub-folder
78: 2. Creates the folder structure manually or via `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/create.sh --subfolder`
79: 3. Copies templates as needed
80: 
81: **Script-assisted example:**
82: 
83: ```bash
84: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/create.sh \
85:   --subfolder specs/<track> \
86:   --topic memory-overhaul \
87:   --level 3+ \
88:   "Wave 1 follow-up"
89: ```
90: 
91: ### Step 4: Path Tracking
92: 
93: Routine saves pass the target spec folder alongside structured JSON.
94: 
95: ---
96: 
97: ## 4. NAMING CONVENTION
98: 
99: - **Sub-folder format**: `{###}-{descriptive-name}` (script-generated or manual)
100: - **Numbers**: 001, 002, 003, etc. (3-digit padded, sequential)
101: - **Name rules**: lowercase, hyphens, 2-3 words (shorter is better)
102: - **Examples**: `001-mcp-code-mode`, `002-api-refactor`, `003-bug-fixes`
103: 
104: ---
105: 
106: ## 5. MEMORY CONTEXT ROUTING
107: 
108: - Spec folder path passed explicitly alongside structured JSON for routine saves
109: - `generate-context.js` refreshes canonical continuity in the specified sub-folder's `implementation-summary.md` `_memory.continuity` block (legacy `[spec]/memory/*.md` writes are retired)
110: - Each iteration has isolated continuity history
111: - Sub-folder creation also provisions isolated `scratch/` directories
112: - Older packets may still contain a root `memory/` directory from before the retirement; current saves write only canonical continuity
113: 
114: ---
115: 
116: ## 6. EXAMPLE USE CASE
117: 
118: ### Manual Sub-Folder Organization
119: 
120: **Scenario:** User wants to organize iterative work within an existing spec folder
121: 
122: 1. **Initial State:**
123:    ```
124:    specs/007-auth-system/
125:    ├── spec.md
126:    ├── plan.md
127:    └── implementation-summary.md
128:    ```
129: 
130: 2. **After Manual Organization:**
131:    ```
132:    specs/007-auth-system/
133:    ├── 001-initial-implementation/    # Original content (manually moved)
134:    │   ├── spec.md
135:    │   ├── plan.md
136:    │   └── implementation-summary.md
137:    └── 002-oauth-addition/            # New work
138:        ├── spec.md
139:        ├── plan.md
140:        └── implementation-summary.md
141:    ```
142: 
143: **Key Points:**
144: - User manually creates and organizes sub-folders
145: - Original content can be moved to a sub-folder if desired
146: - Each sub-folder has independent continuity in its `implementation-summary.md`
147: - Numbering is sequential within the spec folder
148: 
149: ### Step-by-Step Walkthrough
150: 
151: 1. User runs `/spec_kit:complete` or similar
152: 2. Gate 3 asks: "Spec folder?" → User selects **A) Existing**
153: 3. User selects `specs/007-auth-system/`
154: 4. AI suggests: "This folder has existing content. Would you like to organize work in a sub-folder?"
155: 5. If yes:
156:    - User provides sub-folder name: "002-oauth-addition"
157:    - AI helps create the sub-folder with templates
158:    - Continuity saves update the sub-folder's `implementation-summary.md` `_memory.continuity` block
159: 6. If no:
160:    - Continue working in root folder
161: 
162: ---
163: 
164: ## 7. BENEFITS
165: 
166: - Clean separation of iterative work
167: - Preserves all historical work (no data loss)
168: - Independent continuity per iteration
169: - Backward compatible (works with non-versioned folders)
170: - Flexible organization based on project needs
171: 
172: ---
173: 
174: ## 8. PHASES VS VERSIONS
175: 
176: Sub-folder versioning and phases serve distinct purposes:
177: 
178: | Aspect | Sub-Folder Versioning | Phase Decomposition |
179: |--------|----------------------|---------------------|
180: | **Purpose** | Sequential iterations of the same work | Parallel decomposition of different work streams |
181: | **Relationship** | Each version builds on or replaces the previous | Each phase addresses a distinct part of the whole |
182: | **Naming** | `001-original/`, `002-iteration/` | `001-foundation/`, `002-api-layer/` |
183: | **Trigger** | Option A reuse with existing content | Complexity score >= 25 AND level >= 3, or a series parent (`phase-definitions.md` §2) |
184: | **Workflow** | One active version at a time | Multiple phases may be active simultaneously |
185: | **Parent spec** | Optional (root docs may exist) | Required (Phase Documentation Map in parent spec.md) |
186: | **Back-reference** | Not required | Child spec.md references parent via `parent:` metadata |
187: 
188: **Key distinction:** Versions are **temporal** (this work, then that work). Phases are **spatial** (this part and that part, potentially in parallel).
189: 
190: **Version or series parent?** Use a sub-folder version when the follow-up iterates on the packet's own work and the packet's slug still describes it. Use a series parent (`phase-definitions.md` §2) when the follow-up is a different change to the same artifact, because the first packet's slug names only its own change.
191: 
192: Both systems use the same `###-name/` naming convention for child folders and both keep independent canonical continuity (`implementation-summary.md` `_memory.continuity`) per child.
193: 
194: ---
195: 
196: ## 9. GENERATE-CONTEXT.JS INTEGRATION
197: 
198: When using subfolder versioning, the spec-doc record save script (`generate-context.js`) fully supports nested paths.
199: 
200: ### Supported Input Formats
201: 
202: | Input                                  | Resolution                                        |
203: | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
204: | `003-parent/121-child`                 | Resolves to `{specsDir}/003-parent/121-child/`    |
205: | `002-track/022-feature/011-phase`      | Resolves three-level nested packet path           |
206: | `121-child` (bare)                     | Searches all parents, requires unique match        |
207: | `specs/003-parent/121-child`           | Strips prefix, resolves nested                     |
208: | Internal design notes | Strips prefix, resolves nested                     |
209: 
210: ### Continuity Save Location
211: 
212: Canonical continuity is always written to the CHILD folder's `implementation-summary.md`:
213: - `specs/003-parent/121-child/implementation-summary.md` (correct)
214: - `specs/003-parent/implementation-summary.md` (wrong — parent-level, not child)
215: 
216: ### Bare Child Ambiguity
217: 
218: If a child name like `121-audit` exists under multiple parents, the script requires the full path:
219: 
220: ```
221: Error: Ambiguous child folder "121-audit" found in multiple parents:
222:   - <spec-folder>
223:   - specs/005-<user-repo>/121-audit/
224: Please specify the full path: parent/child
225: ```
226: 
227: ---
228: 
229: ## 10. RELATED RESOURCES
230:

232: - [template-guide.md](../templates/template-guide.md) - Template selection, adaptation, and quality standards
233: - level specifications reference - Complete Level 1-3 requirements and migration
234: - [quick-reference.md](../workflows/quick-reference.md) - Commands, checklists, and troubleshooting

199:  -c model_reasoning_effort="medium" \
212:| (nothing specified) | `--model gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort="medium" -c service_tier="fast"` |
213:| "Use gpt 5.5 high fast" | `--model gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort="high" -c service_tier="fast"` |
214:| "Use gpt 5.5 low" | `--model gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort="low" -c service_tier="fast"` (fast stays unless user drops it) |
215:| "Use gpt 5.5 xhigh" | `--model gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort="xhigh" -c service_tier="fast"` |
216:| "Use gpt 6 luna max" | `--model gpt-6-luna -c model_reasoning_effort="max" -c service_tier="fast"` |
217:| "Use gpt 5.6 terra high" | `--model gpt-5.6-terra -c model_reasoning_effort="high" -c service_tier="fast"` |
218:| "Use gpt 6 sol ultra" | `--model gpt-6-sol -c model_reasoning_effort="ultra" -c service_tier="fast"` |
224:`gpt-5.5` at `medium` on the `fast` service tier (`-c service_tier="fast"`) is the skill default for cross-AI delegation. Alternates: `gpt-6-luna` (≤ `max`), `gpt-5.6-terra` / `gpt-6-sol` (≤ `ultra`) — full roster, per-model effort ceilings, and the 8-level effort ladder in [references/providers-and-models.md](references/providers-and-models.md). Set effort with `-c model_reasoning_effort="<level>"` (there is **no `--reasoning-effort` flag**).
241:Git diff review uses the built-in subcommand (no `-p`): `codex exec review "..." --commit HEAD`. Profiles may override `model`, `model_reasoning_effort`, `sandbox_mode`, `approval_policy`. The `.codex/agents/*.toml` files define personas for the interactive multi-agent TUI, NOT the `-p` flag.
247:- **`codex exec` defaults to `--sandbox read-only`** — file-modification tasks silently no-op (the agent plans changes but cannot write them). Pass `--sandbox workspace-write`; for headless no-prompt execution use top-level `-a never` before `exec` or `-c approval_policy=never`.
248:- **`--search` is a top-level flag, not an `exec` flag** — enable live web search as `codex --search exec …` (it precedes the subcommand). On codex ≥ 0.144 `codex exec --search` hard-fails with `unexpected argument '--search'` (older 0.125 builds accepted it), so treat any `exec … --search` example as stale. Without it, `codex exec` has no web access and answers from training data only — every dispatch needing live data (latest versions, repo facts, advisories) MUST use `codex --search exec …`.
250:- **No `--reasoning-effort`, `--reasoning`, or `--quiet` flag exists** — set effort with `-c model_reasoning_effort="<level>"`; capture the last message with `-o file.txt`; capture stderr with `2>&1`.
261:3. Use `--sandbox read-only` for review/analysis/research; `--sandbox workspace-write` for code generation/file modification — `codex exec` defaults to `read-only`, so omitting it causes silent no-op on edit tasks. For unattended approval, put top-level `-a never` before `exec` or set `-c approval_policy=never`.
264:6. **Redirect codex stdin from `/dev/null` on EVERY non-interactive dispatch** — not only inside a `while read` loop, which is the condition this rule used to name and the reason it was skipped. Pattern: `codex exec "$PROMPT" > "$LOG" 2>&1 </dev/null &`. Without `</dev/null`, the backgrounded codex process inherits the loop's stdin (the file after `done < input.jsonl`) and silently consumes the remaining lines — the loop exits after 3-6 iterations with no error. See `references/integration-patterns.md#background-execution` → "Silent Stdin Consumption".
265:7. **Specify model + effort + service tier explicitly** — never rely on caller environment. Default: `--model gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort="medium" -c service_tier="fast"`. Honor user overrides verbatim. Use `high`/`xhigh` for reasoning-heavy tasks (architecture, security, deep planning).
266:8. Route to the appropriate `-p <profile>` when the task matches a specialization (see Section 3 routing table); use `codex exec review` (built-in subcommand) for git diff reviews.
271:11. **Never inject user-level voice/personalization content into AI-orchestrated Codex delegations.** Codex CLI reads user-level voice from `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` (the human's global settings, loaded automatically). When an AI delegates via `codex exec`, the calling AI's own voice rules govern the response — do NOT read `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` and paste into delegation prompts. Keep delegations focused on task/model/sandbox/effort/(spec-folder pre-approval). If the user asks how to make Codex sound more like Claude in *their own* sessions, point to `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` — not any repo asset.
275:15. **Single-dispatch discipline (operator-gated, session-scoped)** — Default: launch ONE cli-* dispatch at a time across the cli-* family (cli-codex, cli-opencode, cli-claude-code). Wait for the dispatched agent's work to return, verify outputs exist, then SIGKILL only the dispatch THIS skill started: capture its PID at launch (`codex exec ... & CODEX_PID=$!`) and kill that captured PID directly plus its own orphan children (`kill -9 "$CODEX_PID" 2>/dev/null; pkill -9 -P "$CODEX_PID" 2>/dev/null`), then apply the same PID-scoped `gtimeout` cleanup. **Never use a blanket `pkill -9 -f "codex exec --model"` pattern** — that matches and kills EVERY running `codex exec` process on the machine, including the operator's unrelated codex sessions. Only launch the next dispatch (this skill OR a sibling) after the prior one is dead and RSS has dropped. **Within a deep-flow session** (deep-review / deep-research): the operator authorizes the whole multi-iteration session at start — iterations chain back-to-back with kill-between as the safety mechanism, NOT a per-iteration confirmation prompt. **Exception (cross-skill parallel)**: when the operator explicitly authorizes N parallel dispatches, run N concurrently — but still SIGKILL each by its own captured PID as its work returns.
276:16. **Set `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1` in the dispatched child's env AND state the exemption in the prompt.** The variable makes the waiver true; it does not make it observable. The reader being waived is a model, and a model cannot see an environment variable, so a child given only the variable still stops to ask the documentation-scope question and writes nothing, at exit code zero. Copy the preamble from [`shared/references/child-dispatch-preamble.md`](../shared/references/child-dispatch-preamble.md) to the top of every non-interactive prompt. when sessions may be launched through the per-session worktree wrapper (`.skilled/bin/worktree-session.sh`). A dispatched `codex exec` is an orchestrated sub-session, not a new top-level session, so it must SHARE the parent's worktree rather than allocate its own. The wrapper checks `AI_SESSION_CHILD` (plus a `git --git-common-dir` structural backstop) and exec's in place when set. Pattern: `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 codex exec ... </dev/null`. Harmless when the wrapper is not in use. See `.skilled/bin/README.md` → "Worktree session isolation".
278:17. **Agent-persona injection (attach identity, not just the task).** Every dispatch composes `{resolved agent persona + task prompt}` — never a bare task. Resolve the persona from the ACTIVE runtime's agent directory per AGENTS.md §9 (`.skilled/agents/<name>.md`, `.claude/agents/<name>.md`, etc. — never hardcode one runtime), and map each subtask to the RIGHT agent (`code`→code, `review`→review, `design`→design, research→`deep-research`, docs→`markdown`), not one default. **Codex has no native persona surface** — `.codex/agents/*.toml` is TUI-only, and `codex exec` / `-p <profile>` load sandbox/effort config, not a persona. So **INLINE** the persona block into the prompt payload on every dispatch, using the same in-payload pattern as the `DESIGN_DISPATCH_MANIFEST` (Rule 14) — the child cannot resolve agent paths by reference. A persona-less dispatch runs the leaf as a generic assistant, silently dropping the agent's tool-scope, verification gates, and output contract. Canonical contract: `../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md` "Persona Injection"; native precedent: `orchestrate.md` "Agent Loading Protocol". Rare exceptions (focused summary for a small-context model, pure-mechanical command) are declared at the dispatch site.
280:18. **Never dispatch `codex exec` from inside a running codex session.** A codex process cannot spawn another codex from inside its own sandbox. The nested child dies at startup with `failed to initialize in-process app-server client: Operation not permitted` (observed 2026-09-02 on codex-cli 0.151.0 under `--sandbox workspace-write`), and the parent reads that as a failed iteration rather than a route violation. So when codex is itself the executor of a deep-loop fan-out lineage or any other orchestrating session, it must do each iteration's work in-process with its own tools and never dispatch a second codex. Grep that exact message to confirm you are hitting this and not a model or network fault.

63: ### Ledger schema (frozen)
64: 
65: One JSON object per line. All ten fields are required strings.
66:

70: | `lane` | `A`, `B` or `C` |

72: | `locator` | Exact text that occurs once in that file and marks the defect |
73: | `defect_class` | One of the eight classes below |
74: | `observed` | What is there now, in one sentence |
75: | `expected_text` | The exact replacement text, or `DELETE FILE`, or `OWNED BY PHASE` when a later phase rewrites the area |
76: | `owner_phase` | `002`, `003`, `004`, `005`, `006` or `041-006` |
77: | `evidence_cmd` | One shell command, run from the repository root |
78: | `evidence_expect` | The exact text or count that command prints while the defect exists |

293: ## AI EXECUTION PROTOCOL
294: 
295: Written for the executing swarm. Follow each rule as written. Where a rule and your own judgment disagree, follow the rule and record the disagreement in `goal.md` section 4.
296: 
297: ### Roles
298: - **Conductor**: one DeepSeek V4.1 Flash max session that is not itself running inside OpenCode, because `cli-opencode` refuses a dispatch from inside OpenCode. It dispatches workers, runs every verify command, edits only this phase folder, and keeps `goal.md` section 4 current.
299: - **Worker**: one `opencode2 run` dispatch on `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max`. One worker does one lane or one baseline run, then stops.
300: - **Reviewer**: one read-only frontier review through `cli-codex` at phase close. It writes nothing.
301: 
302: ### Pre-Task Checklist
303: - [ ] Read this phase's `spec.md`, this plan and `tasks.md` before the first dispatch
304: - [ ] Read `.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/SKILL.md` sections 3 and 4 before composing the first worker command
305: - [ ] Confirm the working directory is the build worktree recorded in `../goal.md` section 4, never the main checkout
306: - [ ] Confirm `opencode2 models --standalone` lists `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`
307: - [ ] Save every brief to `scratch/briefs/<task-id>.txt` before dispatching it
308: 
309: ### Execution Rules
310: 
311: | Rule | Requirement |
312: |------|-------------|
313: | TASK-SEQ | Run tasks in ID order. Tasks marked `[P]` may run together, at most three at once, and only when no two write the same file |
314: | TASK-SCOPE | A worker writes only the paths under ALLOWED WRITE PATHS in its brief |
315: | TASK-VERIFY | The conductor runs the task's verify command and reads both its output and its exit status before marking the task `[x]` |
316: | TASK-LOCATE | Find text by its exact content, never by a line number |
317: | TASK-BANNED | Workers never run `git commit`, `git push`, `git checkout`, `git switch`, `git branch`, `git reset`, `git stash`, `generate-context.js` or `/speckit:save` |
318: 
319: ### Worker Brief Skeleton
320: 
321: Every brief starts with this block, word for word, with the two paths filled in:
322: 
323: ```text
324: GATE 3 IS PRE-RESOLVED. DO NOT ASK THE DOCUMENTATION-SCOPE QUESTION.
325: 
326: You are a non-interactive dispatched worker. AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 and
327: SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 are set in your environment, which this repository's AGENTS.md
328: defines as the autonomous child-dispatch exemption: the spec-folder question is pre-resolved
329: and MUST NOT be asked. No answer can reach you, because nobody is at a prompt.
330: 
331: Your write authority is already bound. The spec folder is:
332:   specs/system-speckit/054-weak-model-spec-authoring/001-template-drift-census-and-baseline
333: 
334: Proceed directly to the work. Do not print A/B/C/D options. Do not stop to confirm anything.
335: A failed edit match means a stale anchor: re-read the file and retry; halt only after three
336: failures on the same file.
337: Your task is complete only when files exist on disk and the verification command has been run.
338: 
339: ROLE: You are a read-only auditor. You read files, run read-only commands and write one
340: result file. Your output is checked line by line by a script.
341: 
342: ALLOWED WRITE PATHS:
343:   <the one file this task names>
344: 
345: BANNED OPERATIONS: git commit, git push, git checkout, git switch, git branch, git reset,
346: git stash, rm, mv, create.sh outside the task's stated command, generate-context.js,
347: /speckit:save, and any edit to a file not listed under ALLOWED WRITE PATHS.
348: ```
349: 
350: The role line is a focused persona summary in place of a full agent file, the small-context exception that `cli-opencode` rule 18 allows. It is declared here as that exception.
351: 
352: ### Dispatch Command
353: 
354: ```bash
355: cd "$WORKTREE" && SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 opencode2 run --standalone \
356:   -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max --format json \
357:   "$(cat "$PHASE/scratch/briefs/$TASK.txt")" </dev/null > "$PHASE/scratch/runs/$TASK.jsonl" 2>&1 &
358: PID=$!; wait "$PID"; kill -9 "$PID" 2>/dev/null; pkill -9 -P "$PID" 2>/dev/null
359: ```

361: `PHASE` is this folder's path and `WORKTREE` is the build worktree. Never kill by a name pattern. Kill only the captured PID.

368: 1. Restore any file the task changed with `git restore --source=<start commit> -- <file>`.
369: 2. Mark the task `[B]` in `tasks.md` with the failing command and the first line of its output.
370: 3. Re-dispatch at most twice with the brief corrected for what failed. After the third failure on the same task, leave it `[B]` and continue with the next task.
371: 4. Stop the phase when two tasks are blocked, and write `STOP` with both task IDs in `goal.md` section 4.

376: ## L3: ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORD
377: 
378: ### ADR-001: Keep only rows that reproduce
379: 
380: **Status**: Accepted
381: 
382: **Context**: A DeepSeek worker asked to find defects will also report things that are not defects.
383: 
384: **Decision**: A lane row enters `ledger.jsonl` only when the conductor runs its `evidence_cmd` on the unchanged tree and the output contains its `evidence_expect`. The `self-contradiction` class has no command, so those rows go to the frontier review instead.
385: 
386: **Consequences**:
387: - Phase 2 receives no row it cannot reproduce.
388: - A real defect the worker described badly is dropped. The frontier review reads the source files again to catch those.
389: 
390: **Alternatives Rejected**:
391: - Trusting lane output as written: it puts unconfirmed findings into a repair phase that edits shared templates.
392: 
393: ### ADR-002: One fixed authoring task, three runs, run in a throwaway track
394: 
395: **Status**: Accepted
396: 
397: **Context**: The baseline must be rerun unchanged in phase 8, and one run of a sampling model is one sample.
398: 
399: **Decision**: The task text in `tasks.md` T009 is frozen. It runs three times per side. Each run creates `specs/zz-bench-authoring/`, and the conductor deletes that directory after measuring.
400: 
401: **Consequences**:
402: - Phase 8 compares like with like and reports a range.
403: - Three runs cannot detect a small effect. Phase 8 reports the range, not a significance claim.
404: 
405: **Alternatives Rejected**:
406: - Measuring by a frontier model's judgment of quality: one model is one opinion, and the five metrics are commands.

58: - **Lane A worker**: reads `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/` except `examples/`.
59: - **Lane B worker**: reads `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/examples/`.

61: - **Conductor**: merges lane files, re-runs evidence, writes `ledger.jsonl`, runs the baseline.

63: ### Ledger schema (frozen)

66: 
67: | Field | Meaning |

70: | `lane` | `A`, `B` or `C` |
71: | `file` | Repository-relative path of the file with the defect |
72: | `locator` | Exact text that occurs once in that file and marks the defect |
73: | `defect_class` | One of the eight classes below |
74: | `observed` | What is there now, in one sentence |
75: | `expected_text` | The exact replacement text, or `DELETE FILE`, or `OWNED BY PHASE` when a later phase rewrites the area |
76: | `owner_phase` | `002`, `003`, `004`, `005`, `006` or `041-006` |
77: | `evidence_cmd` | One shell command, run from the repository root |
78: | `evidence_expect` | The exact text or count that command prints while the defect exists |

315: | TASK-VERIFY | The conductor runs the task's verify command and reads both its output and its exit status before marking the task `[x]` |
316: | TASK-LOCATE | Find text by its exact content, never by a line number |
317: | TASK-BANNED | Workers never run `git commit`, `git push`, `git checkout`, `git switch`, `git branch`, `git reset`, `git stash`, `generate-context.js` or `/speckit:save` |

376: ## L3: ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORD
377: 
378: ### ADR-001: Keep only rows that reproduce
379: 
380: **Status**: Accepted
381: 
382: **Context**: A DeepSeek worker asked to find defects will also report things that are not defects.
383: 
384: **Decision**: A lane row enters `ledger.jsonl` only when the conductor runs its `evidence_cmd` on the unchanged tree and the output contains its `evidence_expect`. The `self-contradiction` class has no command, so those rows go to the frontier review instead.
385: 
386: **Consequences**:
387: - Phase 2 receives no row it cannot reproduce.
388: - A real defect the worker described badly is dropped. The frontier review reads the source files again to catch those.
389: 
390: **Alternatives Rejected**:
391: - Trusting lane output as written: it puts unconfirmed findings into a repair phase that edits shared templates.
392: 
393: ### ADR-002: One fixed authoring task, three runs, run in a throwaway track
394: 
395: **Status**: Accepted
396: 
397: **Context**: The baseline must be rerun unchanged in phase 8, and one run of a sampling model is one sample.
398: 
399: **Decision**: The task text in `tasks.md` T009 is frozen. It runs three times per side. Each run creates `specs/zz-bench-authoring/`, and the conductor deletes that directory after measuring.
400: 
401: **Consequences**:
402: - Phase 8 compares like with like and reports a range.
403: - Three runs cannot detect a small effect. Phase 8 reports the range, not a significance claim.
404: 
405: **Alternatives Rejected**:
406: - Measuring by a frontier model's judgment of quality: one model is one opinion, and the five metrics are commands.

384: **Decision**: A lane row enters `ledger.jsonl` only when the conductor runs its `evidence_cmd` on the unchanged tree and the output contains its `evidence_expect`. The `self-contradiction` class has no command, so those rows go to the frontier review instead.
385: 
386: **Consequences**:
387: - Phase 2 receives no row it cannot reproduce.
388: - A real defect the worker described badly is dropped. The frontier review reads the source files again to catch those.
389: 
390: **Alternatives Rejected**:
391: - Trusting lane output as written: it puts unconfirmed findings into a repair phase that edits shared templates.
392: 
393: ### ADR-002: One fixed authoring task, three runs, run in a throwaway track
394: 
395: **Status**: Accepted
396: 
397: **Context**: The baseline must be rerun unchanged in phase 8, and one run of a sampling model is one sample.
398: 
399: **Decision**: The task text in `tasks.md` T009 is frozen. It runs three times per side. Each run creates `specs/zz-bench-authoring/`, and the conductor deletes that directory after measuring.
400: 
401: **Consequences**:
402: - Phase 8 compares like with like and reports a range.
403: - Three runs cannot detect a small effect. Phase 8 reports the range, not a significance claim.
404: 
405: **Alternatives Rejected**:
406: - Measuring by a frontier model's judgment of quality: one model is one opinion, and the five metrics are commands.

293: ## AI EXECUTION PROTOCOL
294: 
295: Written for the executing swarm. Follow each rule as written. Where a rule and your own judgment disagree, follow the rule and record the disagreement in `goal.md` section 4.
296: 
297: ### Roles
298: - **Conductor**: one DeepSeek V4.1 Flash max session that is not itself running inside OpenCode, because `cli-opencode` refuses a dispatch from inside OpenCode. It dispatches workers, runs every verify command, edits only this phase folder, and keeps `goal.md` section 4 current.
299: - **Worker**: one `opencode2 run` dispatch on `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max`. One worker does one lane or one baseline run, then stops.

302: ### Pre-Task Checklist
303: - [ ] Read this phase's `spec.md`, this plan and `tasks.md` before the first dispatch
304: - [ ] Read `.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/SKILL.md` sections 3 and 4 before composing the first worker command
305: - [ ] Confirm the working directory is the build worktree recorded in `../goal.md` section 4, never the main checkout
306: - [ ] Confirm `opencode2 models --standalone` lists `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`

309: ### Execution Rules
310: 
311: | Rule | Requirement |
312: |------|-------------|
313: | TASK-SEQ | Run tasks in ID order. Tasks marked `[P]` may run together, at most three at once, and only when no two write the same file |
314: | TASK-SCOPE | A worker writes only the paths under ALLOWED WRITE PATHS in its brief |
315: | TASK-VERIFY | The conductor runs the task's verify command and reads both its output and its exit status before marking the task `[x]` |
316: | TASK-LOCATE | Find text by its exact content, never by a line number |
317: | TASK-BANNED | Workers never run `git commit`, `git push`, `git checkout`, `git switch`, `git branch`, `git reset`, `git stash`, `generate-context.js` or `/speckit:save` |
318:

320: 
321: Every brief starts with this block, word for word, with the two paths filled in:
322: 
323: ```text
324: GATE 3 IS PRE-RESOLVED. DO NOT ASK THE DOCUMENTATION-SCOPE QUESTION.
325: 
326: You are a non-interactive dispatched worker. AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 and
327: SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 are set in your environment, which this repository's AGENTS.md
328: defines as the autonomous child-dispatch exemption: the spec-folder question is pre-resolved
329: and MUST NOT be asked. No answer can reach you, because nobody is at a prompt.
330: 
331: Your write authority is already bound. The spec folder is:
332:   specs/system-speckit/054-weak-model-spec-authoring/001-template-drift-census-and-baseline
333: 
334: Proceed directly to the work. Do not print A/B/C/D options. Do not stop to confirm anything.
335: A failed edit match means a stale anchor: re-read the file and retry; halt only after three
336: failures on the same file.
337: Your task is complete only when files exist on disk and the verification command has been run.
338: 
339: ROLE: You are a read-only auditor. You read files, run read-only commands and write one
340: result file. Your output is checked line by line by a script.
341: 
342: ALLOWED WRITE PATHS:
343:   <the one file this task names>
344: 
345: BANNED OPERATIONS: git commit, git push, git checkout, git switch, git branch, git reset,
346: git stash, rm, mv, create.sh outside the task's stated command, generate-context.js,
347: /speckit:save, and any edit to a file not listed under ALLOWED WRITE PATHS.
348: ```

350: The role line is a focused persona summary in place of a full agent file, the small-context exception that `cli-opencode` rule 18 allows. It is declared here as that exception.

355: cd "$WORKTREE" && SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 opencode2 run --standalone \

377: 
378: ### ADR-001: Keep only rows that reproduce
379: 
380: **Status**: Accepted
381: 
382: **Context**: A DeepSeek worker asked to find defects will also report things that are not defects.
383: 
384: **Decision**: A lane row enters `ledger.jsonl` only when the conductor runs its `evidence_cmd` on the unchanged tree and the output contains its `evidence_expect`. The `self-contradiction` class has no command, so those rows go to the frontier review instead.
385: 
386: **Consequences**:
387: - Phase 2 receives no row it cannot reproduce.
388: - A real defect the worker described badly is dropped. The frontier review reads the source files again to catch those.
389: 
390: **Alternatives Rejected**:
391: - Trusting lane output as written: it puts unconfirmed findings into a repair phase that edits shared templates.
392: 
393: ### ADR-002: One fixed authoring task, three runs, run in a throwaway track
394: 
395: **Status**: Accepted
396: 
397: **Context**: The baseline must be rerun unchanged in phase 8, and one run of a sampling model is one sample.
398: 
399: **Decision**: The task text in `tasks.md` T009 is frozen. It runs three times per side. Each run creates `specs/zz-bench-authoring/`, and the conductor deletes that directory after measuring.
400: 
401: **Consequences**:
402: - Phase 8 compares like with like and reports a range.
403: - Three runs cannot detect a small effect. Phase 8 reports the range, not a significance claim.
404: 
405: **Alternatives Rejected**:
406: - Measuring by a frontier model's judgment of quality: one model is one opinion, and the five metrics are commands.

293: ## AI EXECUTION PROTOCOL
294: 
295: Written for the executing swarm. Follow each rule as written. Where a rule and your own judgment disagree, follow the rule and record the disagreement in `goal.md` section 4.
296: 
297: ### Roles
298: - **Conductor**: one DeepSeek V4.1 Flash max session that is not itself running inside OpenCode, because `cli-opencode` refuses a dispatch from inside OpenCode. It dispatches workers, runs every verify command, edits only this phase folder, and keeps `goal.md` section 4 current.
299: - **Worker**: one `opencode2 run` dispatch on `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max`. One worker does one lane or one baseline run, then stops.
300: - **Reviewer**: one read-only frontier review through `cli-codex` at phase close. It writes nothing.
301: 
302: ### Pre-Task Checklist
303: - [ ] Read this phase's `spec.md`, this plan and `tasks.md` before the first dispatch
304: - [ ] Read `.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/SKILL.md` sections 3 and 4 before composing the first worker command
305: - [ ] Confirm the working directory is the build worktree recorded in `../goal.md` section 4, never the main checkout
306: - [ ] Confirm `opencode2 models --standalone` lists `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`
307: - [ ] Save every brief to `scratch/briefs/<task-id>.txt` before dispatching it
308: 
309: ### Execution Rules
310: 
311: | Rule | Requirement |
312: |------|-------------|
313: | TASK-SEQ | Run tasks in ID order. Tasks marked `[P]` may run together, at most three at once, and only when no two write the same file |
314: | TASK-SCOPE | A worker writes only the paths under ALLOWED WRITE PATHS in its brief |
315: | TASK-VERIFY | The conductor runs the task's verify command and reads both its output and its exit status before marking the task `[x]` |
316: | TASK-LOCATE | Find text by its exact content, never by a line number |
317: | TASK-BANNED | Workers never run `git commit`, `git push`, `git checkout`, `git switch`, `git branch`, `git reset`, `git stash`, `generate-context.js` or `/speckit:save` |
318: 
319: ### Worker Brief Skeleton
320: 
321: Every brief starts with this block, word for word, with the two paths filled in:
322: 
323: ```text
324: GATE 3 IS PRE-RESOLVED. DO NOT ASK THE DOCUMENTATION-SCOPE QUESTION.
325: 
326: You are a non-interactive dispatched worker. AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 and
327: SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 are set in your environment, which this repository's AGENTS.md
328: defines as the autonomous child-dispatch exemption: the spec-folder question is pre-resolved
329: and MUST NOT be asked. No answer can reach you, because nobody is at a prompt.
330: 
331: Your write authority is already bound. The spec folder is:
332:   specs/system-speckit/054-weak-model-spec-authoring/001-template-drift-census-and-baseline
333: 
334: Proceed directly to the work. Do not print A/B/C/D options. Do not stop to confirm anything.
335: A failed edit match means a stale anchor: re-read the file and retry; halt only after three
336: failures on the same file.
337: Your task is complete only when files exist on disk and the verification command has been run.
338: 
339: ROLE: You are a read-only auditor. You read files, run read-only commands and write one
340: result file. Your output is checked line by line by a script.
341: 
342: ALLOWED WRITE PATHS:
343:   <the one file this task names>
344: 
345: BANNED OPERATIONS: git commit, git push, git checkout, git switch, git branch, git reset,

376: ## L3: ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORD
377: 
378: ### ADR-001: Keep only rows that reproduce
379: 
380: **Status**: Accepted
381: 
382: **Context**: A DeepSeek worker asked to find defects will also report things that are not defects.
383: 
384: **Decision**: A lane row enters `ledger.jsonl` only when the conductor runs its `evidence_cmd` on the unchanged tree and the output contains its `evidence_expect`. The `self-contradiction` class has no command, so those rows go to the frontier review instead.
385: 
386: **Consequences**:
387: - Phase 2 receives no row it cannot reproduce.
388: - A real defect the worker described badly is dropped. The frontier review reads the source files again to catch those.
389: 
390: **Alternatives Rejected**:
391: - Trusting lane output as written: it puts unconfirmed findings into a repair phase that edits shared templates.
392: 
393: ### ADR-002: One fixed authoring task, three runs, run in a throwaway track
394: 
395: **Status**: Accepted
396: 
397: **Context**: The baseline must be rerun unchanged in phase 8, and one run of a sampling model is one sample.
398: 
399: **Decision**: The task text in `tasks.md` T009 is frozen. It runs three times per side. Each run creates `specs/zz-bench-authoring/`, and the conductor deletes that directory after measuring.
400: 
401: **Consequences**:
402: - Phase 8 compares like with like and reports a range.
403: - Three runs cannot detect a small effect. Phase 8 reports the range, not a significance claim.
404: 
405: **Alternatives Rejected**:
406: - Measuring by a frontier model's judgment of quality: one model is one opinion, and the five metrics are commands.

local declared_level
    declared_level=$(_complexity_get_declared_level "$folder")
    if [[ -z "$declared_level" ]]; then
        RULE_STATUS="pass"
        RULE_MESSAGE="No declared level found in spec.md (using inferred level)"
        return 0
    fi

    # Get content counts
    local story_count scenario_count phase_count task_count
    story_count=$(_complexity_count_user_stories "$folder")
    scenario_count=$(_complexity_count_acceptance_scenarios "$folder")
    phase_count=$(_complexity_count_phases "$folder")
    task_count=$(_complexity_count_tasks "$folder")

    # Define minimum signal thresholds per level.
    # Keep these intentionally conservative to avoid false warnings on current templates.
    local min_phases min_tasks
    case "$declared_level" in
        1)
            min_phases=1
            min_tasks=3
            ;;
        2)
            min_phases=2
            min_tasks=4
            ;;
        3|3+)
            min_phases=2
            min_tasks=5
            ;;
        *)
            # Unknown level - skip checks
            RULE_STATUS="pass"
            RULE_MESSAGE="Unknown level '$declared_level' - skipping complexity checks"
            return 0
            ;;
    esac

    # Check phase count
    if [[ "$phase_count" -lt "$min_phases" ]]; then
        warnings+=("Phases ($phase_count) below minimum ($min_phases) for Level $declared_level")
    fi

    # Check task count
    if [[ "$task_count" -lt "$min_tasks" ]]; then
        warnings+=("Tasks ($task_count) below minimum ($min_tasks) for Level $declared_level")
    fi

    # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

        RULE_MESSAGE="Complexity level consistent with content (Level $declared_level; phases=$phase_count, tasks=$task_count, stories=$story_count, scenarios=$scenario_count)"

        RULE_MESSAGE="No declared level found in spec.md (using inferred level)"
        return 0
    fi

    # Get content counts
    local story_count scenario_count phase_count task_count
    story_count=$(_complexity_count_user_stories "$folder")
    scenario_count=$(_complexity_count_acceptance_scenarios "$folder")
    phase_count=$(_complexity_count_phases "$folder")
    task_count=$(_complexity_count_tasks "$folder")

    # Define minimum signal thresholds per level.
    # Keep these intentionally conservative to avoid false warnings on current templates.
    local min_phases min_tasks
    case "$declared_level" in
        1)
            min_phases=1
            min_tasks=3
            ;;
        2)
            min_phases=2
            min_tasks=4
            ;;
        3|3+)
            min_phases=2
            min_tasks=5
            ;;
        *)
            # Unknown level - skip checks
            RULE_STATUS="pass"
            RULE_MESSAGE="Unknown level '$declared_level' - skipping complexity checks"
            return 0
            ;;
    esac

    # Check phase count
    if [[ "$phase_count" -lt "$min_phases" ]]; then
        warnings+=("Phases ($phase_count) below minimum ($min_phases) for Level $declared_level")
    fi

    # Check task count
    if [[ "$task_count" -lt "$min_tasks" ]]; then
        warnings+=("Tasks ($task_count) below minimum ($min_tasks) for Level $declared_level")
    fi

    # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # 3. RESULTS
    # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    if [[ ${#warnings[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
        RULE_STATUS="pass"
        RULE_MESSAGE="Complexity level consistent with content (Level $declared_level; phases=$phase_count, tasks=$task_count, stories=$story_count, scenarios=$scenario_count)"
    else
        RULE_STATUS="warn"
        RULE_MESSAGE="Content metrics may not match declared Level $declared_level"
        RULE_DETAILS=("${warnings[@]}")
        RULE_REMEDIATION="Review declared level or adjust content to match expectations"
    fi

    return 0
}
